components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-selection-card { width: 100%; min-height: 112px; padding: 19px; border: 1.5px solid #dccbb8; border-radius: 16px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.72); color: var(--ink, #201411); display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; gap: 16px; align-items: center; text-align: left; font-family: 'Manrope Variable', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color .15s ease, transform .15s ease, box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-selection-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: var(--ink, #201411); box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(80,45,26,.11); background: #fff; } .ds-selection-card:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #3b63ff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-selection-card strong, .ds-selection-card small { display: block; } .ds-selection-card strong { font: 800 1.2rem/1 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-selection-card small { margin-top: 5px; color: #765c52; line-height: 1.4; } .ds-selection-icon { width: 54px; height: 54px; border-radius: 14px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #ffe483; font-size: 1.45rem; }

components.css: .ds-story-frame { width: 360px; max-width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 9 / 16; position: relative; overflow: hidden; padding: 23px; border-radius: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; color: var(--ds-text); background: linear-gradient(155deg, var(--ds-bg-from), var(--ds-bg-to)); font-family: 'Manrope Variable', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 28px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.34); } .ds-story-frame::before { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 270px; height: 270px; right: -150px; top: 84px; border-radius: 50%; border: 55px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-accent) 38%, transparent); } .ds-story-frame > * { position: relative; z-index: 1; } .ds-story-frame header { min-height: 28px; padding-bottom: 11px; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-text) 28%, transparent); display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: .65rem; font-weight: 850; letter-spacing: .06em; } .ds-story-clock { margin-top: 35px; font: 900 4.9rem/.9 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.04em; } .ds-story-frame h2 { margin: 10px 0 22px; max-width: 300px; font: 800 2.35rem/.94 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', sans-serif; letter-spacing: -.03em; } .ds-story-frame section { padding: 15px; border-radius: 14px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; background: var(--ds-surface); } .ds-story-frame section span { max-width: 110px; color: var(--ds-muted); font-size: .69rem; font-weight: 750; } .ds-story-frame section strong { font: 850 2.1rem/1 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-story-frame p { margin: auto 0 9px; font: 800 1.03rem/1.17 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-story-frame:focus-within { outline: 3px solid #3b63ff; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
Chat Wrapped feels dealt across a table at a lively house party: saturated card stock, stacked 9:16 scorecards, compact stamps, unapologetically chunky type, and sharp social observations. It is playful and Nigerian-flavoured without becoming unserious; privacy language and conventional controls keep the experience trustworthy while the deck makes every result feel screenshot-worthy.

The application shell is warm paper and dark ink with a single hot action colour. Story cards are a louder world inside that shell: six complete theme sets govern every visible story colour, while directional blur and travel make navigation feel like dealing the next confession. Utility surfaces stay literal, compact, and accessible instead of imitating paper props everywhere.
keyCharacteristics: A house-party confession deck carried through landing, setup, processing, story, paywall, customisation, and sharing.
Warm application paper, near-black brown ink, and a restrained orange action colour.
Saturated 9:16 story cards with theme-disciplined colour and oversized evidence-led typography.
Compact 12–16px corners; pills are reserved for short statuses, toggles, and segmented controls.
Directional blur and horizontal travel are the signature interaction, used only when changing story cards.
Privacy, focus visibility, ownership state, and export eligibility remain explicit at conversion points.

rules.name: The Closed Theme Rule
rules.body: A story slide uses only its active theme variables: background endpoints, surface, text, muted text, accent, and second accent. Application orange, pink, yellow, ink, and paper must never leak into slide content.

rules.name: The Evidence Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every theme must keep headlines, supporting text, and surface content readable against both gradient endpoints and its own surface colour.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Use display type for the reveal and body type for the explanation. Never stack several decorative faces in one card.

rules.name: The Unbroken Card Rule
rules.body: Never compress, crop, or reflow the story into a non-9:16 dashboard tile. Move supporting controls below it.

rules.name: The Earned Lift Rule
rules.body: Reserve the strongest shadows for the proof deck, central story, modal, and drawer. Routine cards stay flatter so the artifact remains dominant.

rules.name: The Preview-Is-Not-Ownership Rule
rules.body: Let people see the final style before buying, but never allow any in-app export or share path to release an unowned theme, font, or Savage treatment.

dos: **Do** make the offer and a working-scale 9:16 proof coexist in the first desktop viewport.
**Do** preserve the 360 × 640 story composition and 1080 × 1920 export result.
**Do** use the active theme’s complete variable set for every story colour.
**Do** keep privacy and name-visibility guidance visible near upload, purchase, customisation, and sharing.
**Do** use directional blur and travel only to communicate story navigation.
**Do** preserve visible focus, Escape, focus trapping/restoration, arrow-key navigation, and reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** let locked themes, fonts, and Savage mode preview live while gating every in-app save, download, and share route until ownership.
donts: **Don't** turn the experience into a generic SaaS hero or analytics-dashboard grid.
**Don't** leak application palette colours into theme-governed story slides.
**Don't** shrink the story card vertically to make desktop controls fit.
**Don't** use decorative motion on routine state changes; most states change directly.
**Don't** use pills as the default shape for buttons, cards, or containers.
**Don't** let a scrim click replace a labelled close control or complete keyboard behavior.
**Don't** treat a visible locked preview as purchased, including browser download fallbacks after Web Share is unavailable.
